title: Missing nodes and missing models, and how to fix them safely

questions.q: Value not in list: ckpt_name: 'x.safetensors' not in []. What does the empty list tell you?
options: That folder has no models the loader can see
The server is out of memory
questions.answer: That folder has no models the loader can see
questions.why: The list is what the menu holds right now, and it is empty.

questions.q: A checkpoint file is 4 KB, and the loader says header too large. What is the likely cause?
options: A saved web page, not a model
questions.answer: A saved web page, not a model
questions.why: We made the same error with a small HTML file. Its first bytes get read as a length.

questions.q: Which fix carries the most risk?
options: Picking another file in the menu
Installing a pack to get a missing node
questions.answer: Installing a pack to get a missing node
questions.why: It runs someone's code with your rights, and may change shared libraries.

questions.q: You have two missing node classes in a graph. How many are reported by a queue?
questions.why: validate_prompt returns at the first class it can't find.

questions.q: ERROR: Could not detect model type. What should you suspect?
options: The file is the wrong kind for this loader
questions.answer: The file is the wrong kind for this loader
questions.why: It opened fine, and isn't recognised as a checkpoint. A LoRA or VAE in the checkpoints folder does this.

questions.q: Why prefer .safetensors over .ckpt from a stranger?
options: A .ckpt can hold pickled Python, which can run code if loaded carelessly
questions.answer: A .ckpt can hold pickled Python, which can run code if loaded carelessly
questions.why: The safetensors docs call it a format for storing tensors safely, as opposed to pickle. ComfyUI's own loader uses weights_only=True, and other tools may not.
